blocks.text: Questions on what this page has just taught. Choose one answer for each.

questions.stem: A meter-reading company sends 6 vans from one yard to 400 homes a day; each van has an 8-hour shift, and some homes are open only in the morning. Which API does the lesson's procedure choose?

options.text: CP-SAT, since the morning-only homes are intervals that may not overlap
options.says: Vans driving between places make routes, question 1; time windows are a dimension of the routing model.

options.text: MathOpt with HiGHS, since every route must come with a proof of optimality
options.says: The procedure sends routes to the routing library first, which takes such rules as parameters.

options.text: The routing library, since vans visit stops and time windows are part of a route
options.says: Right: question 1, vehicles moving between places; the routing guide lists time windows among its variants.

options.text: SimpleMinCostFlow, since each van carries a flow of meter visits out of the yard and back
options.says: A flow decides how much moves on each road; here each van's sequence of stops is the decision.

origin.section: Does It Move Vehicles Between Places? Then the Routing Library

questions.stem: A paint shop orders 15 jobs on its single spray booth; each job has a whole-hour duration and a due date, and lateness is penalized. Which API does the lesson's procedure choose?

options.text: CP-SAT, since jobs on one booth are intervals that must not overlap
options.says: Right: question 4, intervals and sequencing over integers; jobs on one machine are not routes.

options.text: The routing library, since ordering the jobs is a tour through all of them
options.says: The lesson says the order of jobs on one machine has no travel between places and goes to CP-SAT.

options.text: SimpleLinearSumAssignment, since each job is paired with one position
options.says: Lateness depends on the whole sequence, a rule no single (job, position) arc can state.

options.text: MathOpt with GLOP, since due dates turn the model into a linear program
options.says: Every 'this job before that one' choice is a yes/no decision, so it is not an LP; sequencing goes to CP-SAT.

origin.section: Are There Intervals, Sequences or Dense Logic Over Integers? Then CP-SAT

questions.stem: A hospital pairs 20 nurses with 20 shifts, one each, minimizing a whole-number dislike score; no other rule applies. Which API does the lesson's procedure choose?

options.text: CP-SAT, for its Boolean variables
options.says: Question 2 comes before question 4: an exact assignment goes to its special solver first.

options.text: The routing library, for its routes
options.says: No vehicle's sequence of stops is decided; it is a one-to-one pairing.

options.text: KnapsackSolver, for its capacities
options.says: The knapsack solver picks items under capacities; it has no input for pairing two groups one to one.

options.text: SimpleLinearSumAssignment, for its cost table
options.says: Right: question 2, an exact assignment with every rule in the solver's inputs.

origin.section: Is It Exactly an Assignment, a Flow or a Knapsack? Then Its Special Solver, Until One Rule Breaks the Shape

questions.stem: The same nurse pairing gains one rule: the five senior nurses' dislike scores may total at most 12. Nothing is fractional and there is no other logic. Which API does the lesson's procedure choose?

options.text: SimpleLinearSumAssignment, since the cap can be folded into each pair's arc cost
options.says: A cap on a total over several pairs couples arcs; the solver's only inputs are one arc at a time, as the truck rule showed.

options.text: MathOpt, since the cap couples several pairs and only a general model has rows
options.says: Right: question 2 fails like the truck rule; nothing fractional and no dense logic, so question 5: MathOpt.

options.text: The routing library, since a cap on a total is a capacity dimension
options.says: Routing is for vehicles' routes, question 1; nothing here moves between places.

options.text: KnapsackSolver, since a cap on total dislike is one more capacity row
options.says: The problem is still a one-to-one pairing, which the knapsack solver cannot state at all.

origin.section: Is It Exactly an Assignment, a Flow or a Knapsack? Then Its Special Solver, Until One Rule Breaks the Shape

questions.stem: A refinery blends crudes into fuel: tons of each crude may be fractional, and 'use crude C only if the sulfur unit runs' adds a yes/no decision. Which API does the lesson's procedure choose?

options.text: CP-SAT, since the 'only if' rule is native logic, which CP-SAT states best
options.says: Question 3 comes before question 4, and CP-SAT would round the tons and still report OPTIMAL (lesson 4.2.3).

options.text: MathOpt with HiGHS, since tons are continuous and CP-SAT would round them
options.says: Right: question 3; the 'only if' rule becomes an indicator or a big-M row in MathOpt.

options.text: KnapsackSolver, since each crude fills part of the blend's capacity
options.says: The knapsack solver takes whole numbers only and no 'only if' rule.

options.text: The linear solver wrapper with GLOP, since blending is a linear program
options.says: The on/off decision makes it a MIP, and the wrapper's GLOP silently drops integer variables (lesson 4.1.2).

origin.section: Are There Fractional Amounts or Dual Prices? Then a General Model in MathOpt

questions.stem: Finance wants to know how much NPV one more $1k of the 2028 budget would add, read from an LP of the portfolio. Which API does the lesson's procedure choose?

options.text: CP-SAT, since its solver reports a price for every linear row
options.says: CP-SAT returns no dual values; lesson 4.2.3 lists it among the solvers without duals.

options.text: MathOpt with SCIP, since SCIP is the course's second-opinion solver
options.says: SCIP solves an LP through MathOpt but returns no dual values (lesson 4.2.3).

options.text: MathOpt with GLOP or HiGHS, since only LP solvers return dual values
options.says: Right: question 3, dual prices wanted; GLOP, PDLP and HiGHS return them.

options.text: SimpleMaxFlow, since a budget's price is the flow that passes through one arc
options.says: A shadow price is a dual value of an LP row; a max-flow solver returns flows on arcs.

origin.section: Are There Fractional Amounts or Dual Prices? Then a General Model in MathOpt

questions.stem: A lab chooses which of 40 experiments to run within 300 machine-hours and 120 staff-hours, all whole numbers, maximizing a whole-number score; nothing else limits the choice. Which API does the lesson's procedure choose?

options.text: KnapsackSolver, since values, weight rows and capacities state every rule
options.says: Right: question 2; two hour limits are two weight rows, and the knapsack solver takes several capacities.

options.text: SimpleLinearSumAssignment, since each experiment is paired with its hours
options.says: Nothing is paired one to one; experiments are picked under limits.

options.text: The routing library, since machine-hours are a capacity dimension
options.says: There are no vehicles or stops; question 1 says no.

options.text: MathOpt with GLOP, since two capacity rows make it a linear program
options.says: Picking experiments is yes/no, so it is not an LP, and question 2 decides before question 3 anyway.

origin.section: Is It Exactly an Assignment, a Flow or a Knapsack? Then Its Special Solver, Until One Rule Breaks the Shape

questions.stem: A grain cooperative moves whole truckloads from 4 silos to 9 mills along roads with load limits, at least cost per load; the silos hold exactly what the mills need. Which API does the lesson's procedure choose?

options.text: CP-SAT, since truckloads are whole numbers and CP-SAT works over integers
options.says: Question 2 decides first: supplies, demands and capacitated arcs are exactly a min-cost flow.

options.text: The routing library, since trucks drive between the silos and the mills
options.says: The lesson says a problem deciding only how much moves on each road is a flow, even when trucks carry it.

options.text: KnapsackSolver, since each road has a limited capacity to fill
options.says: The knapsack solver picks items under capacities; it has no nodes, supplies or demands.

options.text: SimpleMinCostFlow, since it is supplies, demands and capacitated roads
options.says: Right: question 2, an exact min-cost flow.

origin.section: Is It Exactly an Assignment, a Flow or a Knapsack? Then Its Special Solver, Until One Rule Breaks the Shape

questions.stem: A tree-trimming contractor schedules 25 circuits over 60 days for 3 crews; each job takes whole days, a crew does one job at a time, and some circuits must come before others. Which API does the lesson's procedure choose?

options.text: MathOpt with HiGHS, since start days and precedences are all linear rows
options.says: The 'one job at a time' rule is a disjunction; lesson 4.4.4 measured HiGHS's bound stuck at 0 on such a model.

options.text: pywraplp with SCIP, since new code of this kind starts there
options.says: New code goes to MathOpt; pywraplp is for a model you inherit, and this one is new.

options.text: CP-SAT, since the jobs are intervals that may not overlap on each crew
options.says: Right: question 4; this is GridCap's vegetation schedule, taught in lessons 4.5.1 to 4.5.4.

options.text: The routing library, since it proves the best order of jobs
options.says: The routing library reports ROUTING_SUCCESS for a good route, not a proof of the best one, and these crews' decisions are job days, not routes.

origin.section: Are There Intervals, Sequences or Dense Logic Over Integers? Then CP-SAT

questions.stem: You inherit a `pywraplp` capital-budgeting model that runs on SCIP, and must add a second scenario next month. What does the lesson advise?

options.text: Keep the wrapper and switch it to GLOP, since its LP solvers run fastest
options.says: The wrapper's GLOP drops integer variables silently, which would break a yes/no budgeting model.

options.text: Read and test it, then migrate it to MathOpt before adding to it
options.says: Right: pywraplp is for code you inherit; read it, test it and migrate it (lessons 4.7.1 to 4.7.4).

options.text: Rewrite it in CP-SAT, since every capital-budgeting model is integer-only
options.says: The lesson starts new code in MathOpt and sends an inherited pywraplp model to be read, tested and migrated, not rewritten in another API.

options.text: Port it to KnapsackSolver, since capital budgeting is always a knapsack
options.says: GridCap's selection is a capital budget that is not a knapsack: its must-do, alternative and parent rules break that shape.

origin.section: Everything Else Starts in MathOpt, and pywraplp Is for Code You Inherit
